theories.title: Diffusion-Controlled Coarsening and Phase Ordering in Complex Colloidal Gels
theories.hypothesis: In the absence of buoyancy-driven convection and sedimentation, the coarsening kinetics and structural aging of colloidal gels are dictated entirely by multiparticle diffusion and tunable interparticle interactions, such as critical Casimir forces or depletion attractions. Without gravitational collapse, structural compaction proceeds via a universal scaling law where thermal fluctuations diminish over time as the gel network reorganizes. Polydispersity and non-spherical particle geometry introduce structural frustration that alters the local diffusion coefficients and delays macroscopic collapse. This unified transport mechanism governs both solid-liquid phase separation in metallic alloys and the aging dynamics of soft colloidal networks.
theories.summary: Diffusion-dominated aging and topological coarsening in colloidal and solid-liquid mixtures follow universal scaling laws free from sedimentation.

experiment.title: Polydisperse Gel Coarsening under Tunable Depletion Interactions
experiment.design: Suspend binary mixtures of hard spheres and non-adsorbing polymers in a thermal-control microscopy cell. Expose the sample to controlled thermal quenches to induce depletion-mediated aggregation, and image the 3D spatial evolution using confocal microscopy over extended temporal durations.

theories.title: Capillary-Driven Transport and Phase Separation in Open Porous Media
theories.hypothesis: When two-phase gas-liquid mixtures flow through fixed porous media or open capillary grooves under microgravity, fluid distribution and pressure drop are governed by an intricate balance between capillary pressure gradients, surface wetting properties, and interfacial drag, independent of gravitational body forces. Capillary forces alone can achieve passive phase separation and uniform liquid distribution if the pore size distribution and channel geometry satisfy critical wetting criteria. Deviations from classical Ergun-type pressure drop models occur due to capillary-inertial choking phenomena and phase redistribution at internal corners and junction sites.
theories.summary: Capillary forces and wetting geometry control two-phase flow regimes and phase separation in porous media in the absence of gravity.

experiment.title: Packed Bed Two-Phase Flow Regimes and Pressure Drop Characterization
experiment.design: Pump simultaneous streams of gas and water through packed columns filled with spherical and non-spherical porous packings of varying wettability. Record pressure drops across the bed and use optical imaging to monitor liquid hold-up and bubble migration across different flow rate ratios.
experiment.platform: ISS Packed Bed Reactor Experiment facility

support.title: Capillary Flow Experiment - 2
support.datum: The document supports that capillary forces alone can achieve passive phase separation in microgravity.
support.quote: Studies from CFE-2 may serve to demonstrate how liquids can be efficiently and passively separated from gases in the absence of gravity.

support.title: Capillary Flow Experiment

support.quote: Capillary forces (the interaction of liquid with solid that can draw a fluid up a narrow tube) continue to act in the absence of gravity and can be exploited to control fluid orientation

support.title: Constrained Vapor Bubble
support.datum: The document supports that capillary pressure and interfacial curvature govern fluid behavior under microgravity.
support.quote: On the microscopic scale, the scientific objective is to evaluate the local details of the Kelvin-Clapeyron model of change-of-phase heat transfer under microgravity conditions where the extended Young-Laplace equation predominates.

support.title: Capillary Channel Flow - Critical Velocities Experiment Unit 1

support.quote: A primary objective is determining the critical flow rates at which free surface destabilization ('choking') and gas ingestion occur, emphasizing the capillary-inertial regime.

support.title: Capillary Channel Flow - Critical Velocities Experiment Unit 2
support.datum: The document supports that flow limits in open capillary structures are governed by capillary, viscous, and inertial forces.
support.quote: The central hypothesis for CCF-CV EU2 is that a critical flow rate limit also exists in open capillary channels with wedge and gapped-wedge geometries, and it is governed by the interplay of capillary, viscous, and inertial forces.

support.title: Capillary Channel Flow - Phase Separation Experiment Unit 2

support.quote: The hypothesis underlying CCF-PS EU2 is that specific wedge and gapped-wedge channel designs can passively separate liquid and gas phases due to the complex interplay of capillary and inertial forces.

support.title: Packed Bed Reactor Experiment - 2
support.datum: The document supports that two-phase pressure drop in porous media relies on surface tension and wetting properties, modifying classical Ergun models.
support.quote: It is hypothesized that in microgravity two-phase packed bed flows, pressure drop will be a function of surface tension (captured by a modified Ergun equation), packing wettability and size, and pre-flow conditions.

support.title: Packed Bed Reactor Experiment - Water Recovery
support.datum: The document supports adapting porous media pressure drop models to account for surface properties.
support.quote: While the overarching principles of two-phase flow in porous media apply, the specific material properties of alumina will cause unique flow phenomena, and models can be modified to account for such.

support.quote: By performing capillary flow tests both on Earth and in a microgravity environment, the effects of microgravity on the kinetics of the larger masses of melt flow, and ultimate equilibrium shape of the meniscus will be closely examined.

support.title: Plant Water Management

support.quote: This research was based on the hypothesis that, in microgravity where gravity-driven fluid behavior is absent, capillary forces, surface tension, and geometric design could provide reliable water and nutrient delivery to plant root zones.

support.datum: The document supports that interfacial and capillary forces dominate fluid behavior in microgravity systems.
support.quote: Even with the large millimeter dimensions of the CVB, interfacial forces dominate in these exceedingly small Bond Number systems with small viscous losses.

support.title: Nucleate Pool Boiling eXperiment
support.datum: The document supports that capillary pressure gradients and liquid inertia dominate when gravitational forces are absent.
support.quote: In microgravity conditions, where buoyancy forces become negligible, it is expected that forces arising from the inertia of the liquid, evaporation, and condensation at the vapor-liquid interface, disjoining pressure, capillary pressure gradient, and the resulting flow field will become more dominant.

support.title: Flow Boiling and Condensation Experiment Flow Boiling Module
support.datum: The document supports that microgravity two-phase flow transport is dictated by flow inertia and surface tension.
support.quote: This behavior is drastically altered In the absence of gravity, wherein flow fluid and heat transfer are dictated by flow inertia and surface tension.

support.datum: The document supports that capillary stresses govern droplet behavior when gravitational body forces are minimized.

support.title: Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment-1

support.quote: Researchers derived and identified the key dimensionless parameters governing thermocapillary flow, including the Marangoni number (Ma), Prandtl number (Pr), aspect ratio (Ar), and the novel surface deformation parameter (S).

support.title: Enhanced Particle Tracking in STDC Data and Its Industrial Application of Marangoni Convection
support.datum: The document supports that surface tension and interfacial curvature drive fluid flows independently of gravity.
support.quote: By systematically comparing velocity and pressure fields obtained from these reanalyzed datasets with theoretical perturbation methods and COMSOL Multiphysics computational models, the project seeks to isolate the fundamental role of Marangoni convection and interfacial curvature in driving oscillatory and steady-state flows.

against.title: Packed Bed Reactor Experiment

against.title: Microgravity Investigation of Cement Solidification - Multi-use Variable Gravity Platform
against.datum: The document investigates cement hydration and diffusion-dominant transport under variable gravity rather than gas-liquid two-phase capillary flow.
against.quote: It is hypothesized that under variable reduced gravity conditions different transport phenomena such as buoyancy, sedimentation, and convection are minimized and a more diffusion dominant transport will lead to varying degree of uniformity in distribution ofphases

against.quote: These forces include particle-SLI interaction force, drag force on the particle, gravitational force, Saffman force, and Magnus force. The last three are strongly affected by the level of gravitational acceleration.
